series.name: Operational / Functional Preferences
series.description: Defines deployment, runtime behavior, monitoring, and maintenance preferences informed by tech spec and methodology.

open_ended.text: How should the system be deployed, released, and updated in production?

follow_up_choices.text: Manual deploy — push artifacts, restart services, update on schedule
Automated CI/CD — merged to main triggers build + deploy pipeline
Progressive delivery — feature flags, canary releases, gradual rollout

open_ended.text: What environment and release management strategy should be used?

follow_up_choices.text: Single environment — production only, with local dev
Dev / staging / production — standard promotion pipeline
Ephemeral environments — per-branch previews, review apps

open_ended.text: What logging, monitoring, alerting, and observability infrastructure is needed?

follow_up_choices.text: Minimal — basic logging to stdout, manual check-ins
Standard — structured logging, metrics dashboard, alert on errors
Full observability — traces, logs, metrics; SLO monitoring; on-call rotation

open_ended.text: What configuration and feature management approach should be used at runtime?

follow_up_choices.text: Static config — environment variables, restart to change
Dynamic config — runtime-reloadable config without redeploy
Feature flags + config — separate toggle system with gradual rollout

open_ended.text: What maintenance schedule, upgrade policy, and lifecycle management is expected?

follow_up_choices.text: Firefighting — fix issues as they arise, no scheduled maintenance
Regular maintenance — scheduled patch cycles, dependency updates
Proactive — automated updates, security scanning, continuous improvement

open_ended.text: What is the long-term stewardship plan? Who owns the system after initial delivery?

follow_up_choices.text: Hand-off — delivered to a separate operations team
Build-and-run — the same team owns development and operations
